question_text: 5% of all items coming off a production line are defective. The manufacturer packages the items in boxes of six, and guarantees a refund if more than two items in a box are defective.

subparts.stem: On what percentage of boxes will the manufacturer have to pay a refund?

mark_breakdown.desc: Calculating probability $\approx 0.00223$ and converting to percentage $0.223\%$

subparts.solution:
Let $X$ be the number of defective items.
$n = 6$, so $X = 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5,$ or $6$, and $p = 5\% = 0.05$.
$\therefore X \sim \text{B}(6, 0.05)$
Using technology:
$$P(X > 2) = P(X \ge 3) \approx 0.00223$$
$\therefore$ the manufacturer will have to pay a refund on about $0.00223 \times 100\% \approx 0.223\%$ of boxes.

ai_explanation.concept_rule: A refund is paid when there are more than 2 defective items in a box of 6 items, modelled by a binomial distribution.
step_by_step: Multiply by $100\%$ to express as a percentage: $0.223\%$.

subparts.stem: Patrick purchases 10 boxes. Find the probability that he will get a refund for exactly 1 box.
subparts.solution:
Let $Y$ be the number of boxes refunded.
$n = 10$, so $Y = 0, 1, 2, 3, \dots, 10$, and $p \approx 0.00223$ {from a}
$\therefore Y \sim \text{B}(10, 0.00223)$
$$P(Y = 1) \approx \binom{10}{1}(0.00223)^1(1 - 0.00223)^9 \approx 0.0219$$
So, the probability that Patrick will get a refund for exactly 1 box is about $0.0219$.

ai_explanation.concept_rule: The number of refunded boxes follows a second binomial distribution where the probability of success is the answer from part a.
